title: Compatibility guardrails and upgrade automation for LTS cohorts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a practical compatibility and rollout surface for Redwood's LTS cohorts across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console, plus the automation needed to validate and execute safe upgrades.

Scope: runtime (inference engine, kernel selection, KV cache), public REST/SDK API compatibility, JS/Python SDKs, and Console rollout/upgrade UX. This ticket designs the guardrails, automation flows, and observability hooks; implementation will be split into follow-up tasks.

Design summary: 
- Channel model: introduce explicit channel labels attached to releases (stable-lts, maintenance, transition). Channels are orthogonal to semantic versioning but mapped via release metadata. Stable-LTS receives security + critical fixes for 18 months; Maintenance receives only critical patches and extended support for customers on contracts; Transition releases are used for early staged rollouts with stricter rollback policies.
- Versioning policy: semantic versioning for public surfaces (runtime, API and SDKs). Major version increments require API contract review and cross-surface compatibility checklist. Patch/minor changes must include a compatibility classifier (safe, opt-in-break, break).
- Compatibility matrix: canonical matrix maps runtime ABI, API schema, SDK minor/major compatibility and Console feature flags. Matrix rows: {runtime_v, api_v, sdk_python_v, sdk_js_v, console_v, channel_label, supported_until}. This ticket defines the matrix schema and lenses for automated checks.
- Rollout gates and thresholds: automated preflight must validate: (1) API contract diffs against openapi spec (no breaking changes unless labelled), (2) runtime 99p latency delta < 12% on representative workload, (3) token/unit-cost delta < 6%, (4) golden prompts regression A/B: top-5 BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop < 2% on regulated eval set, (5) end-to-end e2e acceptance tests for customer-configured workflows. Failure of any gate blocks promotion.
- Upgrade choreography: Canary -> Cohort ramp (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) -> Full. Each step requires health windows of 30m-2h depending on cohort size and checks above. For LTS channels, additional manual approval required at 20% transition.
- Automated tooling: 
  - preflight-validator (CI job): runs contract diffs, perf harness, regressions, and emits a compatibility score + artifacts.
  - upgrade-planner (Console feature): suggests candidate cohorts based on usage patterns, region, customer tier and pinning constraints; produces rollout plan with schedule and rollback windows.
  - cohort-orchestrator (runtime service): executes staged rollouts, tracks per-customer metrics, and triggers automatic rollbacks when configured thresholds are crossed.
  - compatibility-advisor (SDK lint): warns and suggests code changes when SDKs are used against mismatched runtimes.
- Observability & SLOs: rollout dashboard (Grafana) per release shows latency percentiles, error rates, cost deltas, and golden prompt regression trends. Integrate Trace-ID propagation to surface failing requests to users in affected cohorts. Automatic incident playbooks are linked from the dashboard.
- Customer pinning & escape hatches: customers can pin to a specific release channel/version; platform provides a fast-path rollback route (re-route to previous variant or force-pinned runtime) with audit log and automated billing reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Channel metadata schema and matrix format documented and stored in runtime repo (confluence + JSON schema).
2) Preflight CI job implemented and wired to runtime and API repos (proof: green run for one non-trivial change).
3) Console upgrade-planner mockup + API for submitting rollout plans to cohort-orchestrator.
4) Observability dashboard skeleton showing canary and cohort metrics.
5) Runbook and approval checklist for LTS promotions.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Strict gates increase review friction and time-to-release; mitigate with parallelized preflight tests and compute budget for perf tests.
- Backcompat guarantees across four surfaces (runtime/API/SDK/Console) are combinatorial; we restrict strong guarantees to Stable-LTS channel and require opt-in for other channels.

Implementation notes and references: 
- Prototype preflight validator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/tree/main/preflight-validator
- Draft matrix spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/LTS-compatibility-matrix
- Perf harness for workload replay: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/112
- Draft console mocks in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Upgrade-Planner-Mockups

Next steps (this ticket): author the matrix schema, create the preflight CI job PR, and wire up a initial Grafana panel for canary metrics. Follow-ups listed below.
